description: Hash material recovered from the operator's own CTF, lab and writeup trees (Writeups_Vulnquest HMV/HTB/THM, vulnquest, nexshell, vulnquest222). A full scan of 6840 writeup documents plus 7927 workspace files found only three genuine crackable-hash artefacts: one NTLM hash dumped with secretsdump on HTB Forest and two real JWTs. Bare 32-hex user.txt lab flags were deliberately excluded because they are not password hashes. Plaintexts are omitted where they were never recovered in the source material.

cases.name: NTLM
cases.notes: Domain Administrator NTLM hash extracted with Impacket secretsdump after granting svc-alfresco DCSync rights (Writeups_Vulnquest tree, forest.md:73). The hash is used directly for pass-the-hash; it was never cracked to a plaintext, so this is an identification-only case.

cases.name: JWT (JSON Web Token)
cases.notes: Unsigned ('alg':'none') admin JWT used by the API enumeration plugin in the nexshell project. Included because it exercises the empty-signature branch of the JWT pattern.

cases.name: JWT (JSON Web Token)
cases.notes: HS256 JWT recorded in the local AEGIS notes; the writeups document cracking this format with 'hashcat -m 16500 jwt_token.txt common_secrets.txt'. No signing secret was recovered.
